RemoteFetch.description: Who materialises a remote on disk: `strata` (default) fetches it, `external` means CI or the developer already checked it out and strata only reads it. Use `external` with the real `type` (for example `git` plus the pinned `reference`) when a pipeline clones the repository itself.

RemoteType.description: What kind of source a remote is: `git` (a git repository), `oci` (an OCI registry serving images, Helm charts or other artifacts), `helm` (a Helm chart repository index) or `local` (a directory inside the solution). Who fetches the remote is a separate setting, `fetch`.

SolutionDiscoveryModel.description: Tuning for how strata finds documents under the solution root. Only `exclude` exists: add patterns for folders that hold strata-shaped YAML which must not be loaded, such as a `templates/` or `examples/` folder with placeholders.

exclude.description: Glob patterns matched against each path relative to the solution root, POSIX-style (e.g. 'templates/**', 'examples', '*.generated.yaml'). A matching directory is not descended into. Added to the loader's built-in ignores, never replacing them. Note: these are fnmatch-style globs, not full gitignore syntax — there is no negation ('!') and no leading-slash anchoring.

SolutionRemoteModel.description:
A named remote source of modules, charts or files, referenced elsewhere as `@<name>/<path>` (for example `source: @infra/modules/network`).

A remote only says where the source is, at which ref and how to authenticate. What to take from it is chosen where it is used. Declaring a source once here gives one place to rotate credentials, one place to redirect to a mirror, and a single pinned ref per repository for the whole solution.

Rules:
- Type `git` needs exactly one of `reference` (pin a branch, tag or commit SHA) and `path` (a checkout someone else already placed on disk).
- `path` is only valid for type `git`. It implies `fetch: external`, so `fetch: strata` and `integration` are not allowed with it. It is resolved from the solution root and may use `..` or be absolute.
- `reference` is not allowed for type `helm` or `local`; pick chart versions where the chart is used (`chart_version`).
- For type `oci`, `reference` is required when the remote serves a non-chart artifact (pin one tag or digest) and optional when it only serves charts.
- Type `local`: `url` is a path relative to the solution root without `..`, and `integration` and a non-default `fetch` are not allowed.
- `url` must not embed credentials or start with `-`; put credentials in an Integration and name it in `integration`.

name.description: Remote name, used as the `@<name>` prefix wherever the remote is referenced (for example `@infra/modules/network`). Required.

type.description: What kind of source this is: git, oci, helm, or local

url.description: Remote location: a URL for git/oci/helm, or a solution-relative path for 'local'.

reference.description: The ref every artifact of this remote is taken at: a git branch, tag or commit SHA, or an OCI tag or digest. Required for `git`. For `oci`, required when the remote serves a real image or blob (pinned at one immutable digest) and optional when it only serves Helm charts, where the version is chosen per chart with `chart_version`. Not allowed for `helm` or `local`.

path.description: Where a pipeline or developer already checked this git repository out. Relative to the solution root (the folder holding `strata.yaml`), for example `repos/iac-int-deployment` or, for a checkout beside the solution, `../iac-int-deployment`; or an absolute path. Strata reads it there and never clones it. Use instead of `reference` when the pipeline owns the ref; implies `fetch: external`.

fetch.description: Who materialises this remote on disk: 'strata' (default) fetches it, 'external' means CI or the developer already checked it out and strata must only read it. Use 'external' instead of misdeclaring the type when a pipeline clones the repo itself.

integration.description: Name of an Integration providing credentials for this remote (must declare the 'sources' capability). Omit for public/unauthenticated remotes and for type 'local'. Credentials are never inline here — Integration is strata's single credential mechanism.

SolutionSpecModel.description:
Solution specification: where Configuration lives, and what this solution is composed of.

Rules:
- Remote names must be unique, because the name is how `@<name>/...` references are resolved.

configuration.description: Solution-relative path to the Configuration document(s) — either a single file or a directory whose 'kind: configuration' documents are all merged. Defaults to 'config', which is what real solutions use. Overridden by the CLI's --config-file/--config-path.

remotes.description:
Named remote artifact sources (git/oci/helm/local), referenced elsewhere as '@<name>/<path>'

Rules:
- Type `git` needs exactly one of `reference` (pin a branch, tag or commit SHA) and `path` (a checkout someone else already placed on disk).
- `path` is only valid for type `git`. It implies `fetch: external`, so `fetch: strata` and `integration` are not allowed with it. It is resolved from the solution root and may use `..` or be absolute.
- `reference` is not allowed for type `helm` or `local`; pick chart versions where the chart is used (`chart_version`).
- For type `oci`, `reference` is required when the remote serves a non-chart artifact (pin one tag or digest) and optional when it only serves charts.
- Type `local`: `url` is a path relative to the solution root without `..`, and `integration` and a non-default `fetch` are not allowed.
- `url` must not embed credentials or start with `-`; put credentials in an Integration and name it in `integration`.

description: The solution manifest, `strata.yaml`, at the root of every strata solution. It names the solution, points to the Configuration (`spec.configuration`) and declares the remotes (git, OCI, Helm or local sources) that other documents reference as `@<name>/<path>`. One per solution.

apiVersion.description: API version for the solution manifest

spec.description:
Solution specification (configuration pointer, remotes)

Rules:
- Remote names must be unique, because the name is how `@<name>/...` references are resolved.
